correctness.rationale: Averaging by simultaneous page permutations and layer exchange preserves the centered-projector norm upper bound and feasibility, and yields exactly three off-diagonal weights. Resolving layer parity and page differences gives the two nonstationary page-difference eigenvalues 1−b and 1−b−2c (each multiplicity m−1), the even mean eigenvalue 1−(m+1)b, and the odd 2-by-2 block in RESULT.md. In the odd block the off-diagonal is √m b and the diagonal is (1−2a−mb,1−b−2c), so the lower bound is max(1−b,√m b). At m=2 its unique minimum has b=√2−1. Equality in the odd-block norm bound forces both diagonals to vanish, giving the claimed a and c and a feasible optimum. At m≥3 the degree constraint forces μ≥T=1−1/m. Taking b=1/m, a=0, c=T/2 attains it since 1/√m≤T. Any invariant optimum must have b=1/m and a=0. The remaining odd block has diagonal (0,T−2c) and its norm is at most T exactly when |T−2c|≤T−1/(mT), giving the stated feasible interval and also bounding the odd differences. The central edge entry is invariant under averaging even for a non-invariant P, and the nonnegative hub holds average to zero when m≥3, so both holds must vanish. value.rationale: This exact optimization reveals that an allowed communication edge must be used at two pages and must be suppressed in every optimum from three pages onward. It quantifies non-factorization on a natural graph product and distinguishes the complete invariant optimizer interval from the conclusions valid without invariance. These are design constraints not supplied by a generic SDP formulation or the spectrum of a fixed product walk.
